BVX.0089.d: Phillips & Huntley's [[storyform|Storyform]] engine: a story as one [[story-mind|Story Mind]] examining a problem through four [[throughlines|Throughlines]]. The Command's RULED story spine; every rival plot model in the library maps onto it as a lens.

BVX.0175.d: Robert McKee's *Story*: the scene-level engine beneath Dramatica's signpost floor. Source of [[the-gap|the Gap]], the [[value-turn|value turn]], and the [[controlling-idea|Controlling Idea]].

BVX.0236.d: Shawn Coyne's editorial X-ray: the [[five-commandments|Five Commandments]] recurring fractally at every unit from beat to global story, plus the [[foolscap|Foolscap]] intake and the genre [[genre-clover|five-leaf clover]].

BVX.0193.d: John Truby's organic-body model: a story grows from one [[designing-principle|designing principle]] through the [[twenty-two-steps|22 steps]] to a hero's [[self-revelation|self-revelation]].

BVX.0163.d: Blake Snyder's page-keyed commercial template: the [[beat-sheet|Beat Sheet]] (BS2), 15 fixed beats over ~110 pages, laid out on [[the-board|the Board]].

BVX.0191.d: John Truby's genre theory: fourteen [[the-fourteen-genres|fourteen genres]], each a [[moral-argument|moral argument]] proved through a fixed chapter schema, hero, opponent, and story world.

BVX.0576.d: Jule Selbo's screenwriting-craft genre text: genre as a contract built from [[the-icm|the ICM]], one [[overriding-genre|overriding genre]] stacking [[supporting-genre|supporting genres]], scored by percentage of scenes.

BVX.0580.d: Steve Neale's institutional counter-weight: genre as a process among industry, critics, and audience, run through [[the-inter-textual-relay|the inter-textual relay]] and [[two-verisimilitudes|the two verisimilitudes]].

BVX.0581.d: The field's own reference guide: three incompatible traditions for what a genre is, resolving in Miller's [[typified-social-action|typified social action]], [[uptake|uptake]], and [[meta-genre|meta-genre]].

BVX.0614.d: Tzvetan Todorov's structuralist account of genre by reader position: [[the-hesitation|the hesitation]] between a natural and supernatural explanation, and its [[resolution-mode|resolution mode]].

BVX.0599.d: Farah Mendlesohn's four categories, sorted by [[delivery-mode|delivery mode]]: [[portal-quest|portal-quest]], [[immersive-fantasy|immersive fantasy]], intrusion, liminal.

grand-argument-story.d: A story conceptually complete: every approach to one problem tried through four [[throughlines|throughlines]] until one is proven best. Dramatica's scope claim, not every story qualifies ([[BVX.0089]]).

story-mind.d: The premise that a complete story models one mind's problem-solving process, holistic not sequential. The generative claim under the [[grand-argument-story|Grand Argument]] ([[BVX.0089]]).

storyform.d: The complete, locked blueprint of structural and dynamic answers, independent of the specific events that dramatize it. Two unrelated plots can share one storyform ([[BVX.0089]]).

throughlines.d: Overall Story (they), Main Character (I), Impact Character (you), Relationship Story (we): four seats around one problem, each holding a different Class. No rival model has all four ([[BVX.0089]]).

signpost.d: A fixed structural checkpoint, one per throughline, four per form, sixteen across a complete storyform. A [[journey|Journey]] carries a throughline between two signposts ([[BVX.0089]]).

journey.d: The transition between two [[signpost|Signposts]] on one throughline; three journeys per throughline complete the four-signpost chain ([[BVX.0089]]).

driver-dynamic.d: Action or Decision: which kind of event precipitates a turn. A story's driver matches at both the inciting event and the resolving event ([[BVX.0089]]). OXO's ruled story-level Driver is Action.

limit-dynamic.d: Timelock or Optionlock: whether tension comes from a closing clock or a shrinking set of options ([[BVX.0089]]).

outcome-dynamic.d: Success or Failure, measured objectively against the Overall Story goal, independent of [[judgment-dynamic|Judgment]]. OXO is ruled Failure ([[BVX.0089]]).

judgment-dynamic.d: Good or Bad, measured subjectively against the Main Character's personal fulfillment. Combines with [[outcome-dynamic|Outcome]] into one of four endings. OXO is ruled Good ([[BVX.0089]]).

crucial-element.d: The single Element the Main Character shares with the Overall Story, the hinge between the objective and subjective arguments. Structural position, not plot centrality ([[BVX.0089]]).

the-gap.d: McKee's engine: a minimal action provokes a world reaction bigger than expected, and the gap between what was expected and what was necessary is where the [[value-turn|turn]] lives. It does not close, it reopens bigger ([[BVX.0175]]).

value-turn.d: A value-charged condition flips polarity, plus to minus or the reverse. No turn, no scene. The scene-level minimum, R2 floor of the [[ladder|scale ladder]] ([[BVX.0175]]).

controlling-idea.d: One sentence, Value plus Cause, describing how and why life changes from the story's beginning condition to its end. Provable backward from the [[climax|Climax]] ([[BVX.0175]]).

turning-point.d: A scene's reversal, producing surprise, curiosity, insight and new direction. Coyne's taxonomy splits it into action or revelation ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

crisis.d: The Obligatory Scene: an irreconcilable-goods decision at maximum pressure, no second chance. Never an easy choice ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

climax.d: A value swing at maximum charge, absolute and irreversible, with or without irony. The protagonist's choice must happen on stage ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

resolution.d: The unit's close: subplot cleanup, spread of effects, or a courtesy to the audience. Must state what the [[climax|Climax]] means, not recap what happened ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

inciting-incident.d: The event that radically upsets life's balance, causal or coincidental, opening the chain the [[five-commandments|Five Commandments]] complete ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

progressive-complications.d: The Gap reopening at increasing risk, passing points of no return; complications must trend up, never retreat to a spent magnitude ([[BVX.0175]]).

five-commandments.d: [[inciting-incident|Inciting Incident]] → Progressive Complication → [[crisis|Crisis]] → [[climax|Climax]] → [[resolution|Resolution]]: every unit of story from beat to global story carries all five, fractally ([[BVX.0236]]).

foolscap.d: A one-page diagnostic: Genre, conventions and obligatory scenes, point of view, objects of desire, controlling idea, and the Hook/Build/Payoff arc. Six questions, one screen ([[BVX.0236]]).

obligatory-scene.d: A must-happen beat that pays off a genre's promise. Missing one means the story hasn't fulfilled its contract with the reader, no exemption for literary ambition ([[BVX.0236]]).

genre-clover.d: Time, Reality, Style, Structure and Content genres: five independent audience-expectation axes nourishing one Global Story. Missing any leaf's promise breaks the contract ([[BVX.0236]]).

best-bad-choice.d: One of Coyne's two crisis shapes: choosing the least-bad of two negatives. The other is [[crisis|irreconcilable goods]] ([[BVX.0236]]).

designing-principle.d: A one-line strategy, not a genre template, that the whole story grows from: story process plus original execution. Distinguishes a premise (what happens) from what makes a story original ([[BVX.0193]]).

self-revelation.d: The hero's awareness of his own need; the hero cannot know it at the start, or the story is already over. Strongest when paired with a [[ghost|double reversal]] in the opponent ([[BVX.0193]]).

ghost.d: An unresolved event from the hero's past acting as a counterdesire, "sailing with a corpse in the cargo." Truby's name for the WOUND layer, dramatized structurally rather than dumped as backstory ([[BVX.0193]]).

character-web.d: All characters connect via four channels: story function, archetype, theme, opposition. A character is defined by who he is not, never built in isolation ([[BVX.0193]]).

four-corner-opposition.d: Hero plus three opponents pushed to distinct value-corners, each attacking the hero's weakness a different way. Multiplies conflict from linear to a web ([[BVX.0193]]).

twenty-two-steps.d: The seven key steps (weakness/need → desire → opponent → plan → battle → self-revelation → new equilibrium) expanded to production detail. Every 22-step story is still a seven-step story underneath ([[BVX.0193]]).

revelations-sequence.d: Reveals must be logical, build in intensity, and come at increasing pace; the strongest reveal is a reversal. Plot's real spine is what the audience learns and when ([[BVX.0193]]).

passageway.d: A liminal threshold between subworlds (rabbit hole, wardrobe, mirror) that signals a rules-change on crossing. Has no home in the setting system's four axes or twelve layers yet, flagged OPEN ([[BVX.0193]]).

the-board.d: A four-row corkboard divided by act (Act One / Act Two-A / Act Two-B / Act Three), index cards per scene, roughly 40 cards. A pre-writing planning tool, not the script itself ([[BVX.0163]]).

beat-sheet.d: Fifteen beats pinned to specific pages of a ~110-page script: Opening Image, [[theme-stated|Theme Stated]], Catalyst, Break Into Two, Midpoint, All Is Lost, Break Into Three, Final Image and more ([[BVX.0163]]).

theme-stated.d: Beat 2, page 5: an offhand line voicing the want-versus-need argument the rest of the script proves or disproves, before the hero understands it ([[BVX.0163]]).

midpoint-all-is-lost.d: A matched, opposite-charge pair at pages 55 and 75: a false victory pairs with a false defeat and vice versa. All Is Lost always carries a whiff of death ([[BVX.0163]]).

ten-genres.d: Snyder's mechanism-based genre wheel: Monster in the House, Golden Fleece, Out of the Bottle, Dude with a Problem, Rites of Passage, Buddy Love, Whydunit, Fool Triumphant, Institutionalized, Superhero ([[BVX.0163]]).

ladder.d: The Command's container hierarchy for plot units: [[r1-beat|R1 BEAT]] → [[r2-scene|R2 SCENE]] → [[r3-sequence|R3 SEQUENCE]] → [[r4-act|R4 ACT]] → [[r5-story|R5 STORY]]. plot_systems occupies these containers, it never invents a second hierarchy.

r1-beat.d: One exchange, action met by reaction: something tried, something answered, something now slightly different. Only the value micro-shift is required here, not the full [[five-commandments|Five Commandments]].

r2-scene.d: The smallest container that turns: a [[value-turn|value turn]] and all five commandments present. The scene-level floor of plot ([[BVX.0175]], [[BVX.0236]]).

r3-sequence.d: A chain of scenes answering one dramatic question, usually replaced by a worse one when it resolves.

r4-act.d: One throughline's [[signpost|signpost]], turned by a [[driver-dynamic|driver]]; all four throughlines advance one signpost per act.

r5-story.d: The whole storyform: all four throughlines complete, [[outcome-dynamic|Outcome]] and [[judgment-dynamic|Judgment]] delivered.

p1-address.d: Where a plot unit sits on the [[ladder|scale ladder]]: IP.form.act.sequence.scene.beat. Writes the `address` field.

p2-driver.d: What precipitates the turn, an action or a decision. Fed by Dramatica's [[driver-dynamic|Driver]] dynamic and McKee's inciting incident / crisis decision.

p3-value-in.d: What value is charged, at what polarity, entering the unit. Fed by McKee's value-charged condition and Coyne's [[inciting-incident|Inciting Incident]].

p4-turn.d: The mechanism that flips the value: [[the-gap|the Gap]], the [[five-commandments|commandment chain]], or Truby's plan/battle step.

p5-value-out.d: The value's polarity on exit, and whether the charge is ironic. Fed by McKee's [[value-turn|value turn]].

p6-signpost-seat.d: Which throughline's [[signpost|signpost]] or [[journey|journey]] this unit serves, in which act. Fed by Dramatica and the [[ladder|ladder]]'s R4.

p7-reveal.d: What the audience or a character learns here, and whether it reverses expectation. Fed by Truby's [[revelations-sequence|revelations sequence]] and Coyne's [[turning-point|turning-point taxonomy]].

p8-collision.d: Which character times setting (or character times character) row fires to produce this unit's friction. Writes `collision_row`, e.g. L9xS9. See [[collision-engine|the collision engine]].

p9-stakes.d: How this unit's risk or cost compares to the last one; must trend up. Fed by McKee's [[progressive-complications|progressive complications]] and Coyne's invariant 5.

p10-genre-obligation.d: Which reader-contract obligation this unit discharges, if any. Fed by Coyne's [[obligatory-scene|obligatory scenes]] and Snyder's [[ten-genres|10 genres]] and 15 beats.

p11-time.d: The order told versus the order happened; the discourse texture. Genette's duration, carried in the [[scene-card|Scene Card]].

p12-function.d: What this unit does for the [[grand-argument-story|Grand Argument]], independent of P1 to P11. Fed independently from the storyform, keyed by [[storyform-id|storyform_id]]; mirrors L12 and S12 FUNCTION.

plot-axis-scale.d: Plot units occupy the containers already ruled on the [[ladder|scale ladder]]; plot_systems adds only what happens inside a container, never a new size class.

plot-axis-turn.d: What changes inside a unit: McKee's [[value-turn|value turn]], Coyne's polarity, and [[the-gap|the Gap]] as the mechanism forcing it.

plot-axis-function.d: What a plot unit does for the argument: Signpost, Journey, Setup/Payoff, [[p7-reveal|Reveal]], Reversal, Escalation.

plot-axis-drive.d: Drivers and act turns: Dramatica's [[driver-dynamic|Driver]], McKee's Inciting Incident / Crisis, Coyne's fractal recurrence, Snyder's page-keyed beats.

plot-card.d: The notation slot for one plot unit, paired to the [[scene-card|Scene Card]]: driver, value-in, turn, value-out, signpost seat, reveal, collision, stakes delta, genre obligation, time, function.

plot-slice.d: The twelve-layer P1 through P12 schema, mirror of the 12-Layer Character Database and the [[setting-slice|Setting Slice]]. See [[p1-address|P1]] through [[p12-function|P12]].

collision-engine.d: The mechanism producing a scene's friction from a character-layer times setting-layer row, e.g. L9 EROS times S9 ALLURE. Fires [[p8-collision|P8 COLLISION]] and the [[scene-card|Scene Card]]'s `collision` field.

storyform-id.d: The key binding P12/L12/S12 FUNCTION records to one locked [[storyform|storyform]]. A plot unit with no storyform link may run P1 through P11 only.

s1-body.d: Physical fabric: geography, terrain, architecture, dimensions, materials, layout. Mirrors L1 CORE.

s2-weather.d: Climate, seasons, light, temperature, atmosphere; the place's rhythms. Mirrors L2 VITAL. A canon-thin, authorable gap for DCUS.

s3-sensorium.d: How a place meets the senses: soundscape, smellscape, texture, palette, the presentation surface. Mirrors L3 SOCIAL.

s4-law.d: The rules that bind: governance, institutional mechanics, permission and forbiddance systems. Mirrors L4 WILL.

s5-scar.d: Damage in the fabric: ruins, erasures, renames, sanded-off strata, what was demolished. Mirrors L5 WOUND.

s6-economy.d: What fuels a place: resources, money, flows, traffic, who feeds and powers it. Mirrors L6 DRIVE.

s7-founding.d: Origin: who built it, why, the founding stack, the deep history. Mirrors L7 ORIGIN.

s8-habit.d: Attachment architecture: patterned life, rituals, routines, belonging gradients, insider/outsider. Mirrors L8 IMPRINT.

s9-allure.d: A place's erotics: what it promises, what draws people in, its glamour and seduction. Mirrors L9 EROS.

s10-underside.d: What a place represses: hidden zones, the unspoken, basements literal and social, what surfaces under pressure. Mirrors L10 SHADOW.

s11-vector.d: Trajectory: where a place is going, bloom, rot, collapse, redemption; feeds the setting arc. Mirrors L11 DESTINY.

s12-function.d: Storyform binding, fed from the spine independent of S1 to S11: which throughline Domain the place embodies, its argument role, its charge, and its narrative_invariant set. Mirrors L12 FUNCTION.

setting-axis-scale.d: Places nest: spot to room to site to locale to settlement to region to world to cosmos. Address form DCUS.campus.hall3.room12.

setting-axis-strata.d: What a place is made of: the twelve layers of the [[setting-slice|Setting Slice]], S1 through S12.

setting-axis-function.d: What setting does: Anchor, Characterize, Pressure, Mood, Argue, Afford. A scene deploys one or two modes deliberately.

setting-axis-time.d: A slice is the baseline; states are dated overlays keyed to ladder addresses. The setting arc is the sequence of states.

scene-card.d: The R2 notation, ten fields on one screen: address, setting, active strata, function mode, sensorium, commandments, [[value-turn|value turn]], duration, telling, threads, invariants, collision, exit state. Paired to the [[plot-card|Plot Card]].

setting-slice.d: The twelve-layer S1 through S12 schema, architectural twin of the 12-Layer Character Database. See [[s1-body|S1]] through [[s12-function|S12]].

sitrep.d: The full board, cold start. Spoken, it flushes the Ready Rack and delivers blocks 0 to VII in fixed order.

dope-sheet.d: The standing status page for one BOLO, the five-paragraph order with the next action on top, plus the log. This TM page is a sibling standing-page type beside it.

boresight.d: The understanding check before delivery: readback, the read, clarifying questions only. Nothing builds until it clears.

soi.d: Signal Operating Instructions: the BREVITY's book, search, A to Z, by section, the dictation codebook.

sop.d: SOP.md, the canonical home of every comms code and session protocol. On any conflict with memory, the file wins.

smeac.d: Situation, Mission, Execution, Administration and Logistics, Command and Signal. A BOLO status page and this TM page's calls table both borrow its shape.

bolo.d: A tasking captured in BOLO.md the turn it is spoken. Be On the Lookout, named for the bolas.

command.d: The whole operation under HOTLINE ACTUAL: BLACK, ORANGE and OPERATOR together.

plot-systems-domain.d: The sibling top-layer domain beside the setting system: events, turns, the twelve-layer [[plot-slice|PLOT SLICE]], and the [[plot-card|PLOT CARD]] notation. See TM 04.

l1-core.d: The first character layer: cognition and identity, how the person thinks and who they take themselves to be. Chart feed: Sun and Mercury.

l2-vital.d: The second layer: the body and its presentation, energy, health, how the person reads at first sight. Chart feed: Mars and the Ascendant.

l3-social.d: The third layer: the person in public, status, manners, the mask worn among others.

l4-will.d: The fourth layer: discipline, agency, what the person can make themselves do. Chart feed: Saturn.

l5-wound.d: The fifth layer: the formative injury and the armor built over it; the loss that explains the [[l6-drive|drive]]. Chart feed: the Moon and Chiron.

l6-drive.d: The sixth layer: want versus need, the super-objective, what the person is reaching for and why. Chart feed: the Sun's house and Jupiter.

l7-origin.d: The seventh layer: birth context, family, class, the place and time the person came from. Chart feed: the IC and the fourth house.

l8-imprint.d: The eighth layer: acquired habits, passions, pastimes, the marks experience left.

l9-eros.d: The ninth layer: sexuality and intimacy, desire profile, shame index, the erotic register. Chart feed: Venus, Mars and the eighth house.

l10-shadow.d: The tenth layer: what the person cannot see in themselves, the self-delusion gap, the counter-will. Chart feed: the twelfth house and Pluto.

l11-destiny.d: The eleventh layer: trajectory and vector, where the arc is taking the person, the transit calendar. Chart feed: the Midheaven and the nodes.

l12-function.d: The twelfth layer: the person's job in the story, the Dramatica archetype or function, the throughline seat. Binds the character to the [[grand-argument|argument]].

twelve-layer-character.d: The Command's character system: twelve layers from [[l1-core|CORE]] to [[l12-function|FUNCTION]], three tiers (primary layers, secondary derivations, numeric variables), derived statistics and flag triggers, instanced per character as a vertical slice. The setting slice (S1 to S12) and the plot slice (P1 to P12) mirror its form.

vertical-slice.d: One character instanced through all twelve layers and three tiers, with its structured data block; Victoria Midnight is the proof instance.

tier-1.d: The primary layers of the character slice, sourced directly from canon and ruled by Papi.

tier-2.d: The secondary layers, derived from Tier 1 by the integration protocol.

tier-3.d: The numeric variables and flags computed from Tiers 1 and 2 (the derived statistics, the flag trigger conditions).

derived-statistic.d: A number computed from the slice's variables by a stated formula, such as armor index or satisfaction cycle truncation.

flag-trigger.d: A condition over the slice's variables that, when met, raises a flag the story engine reads.

structured-data-block.d: The machine-readable block at the end of a character slice: every variable and derived statistic as fields.

BVX.0196.d: David Corbett's five cornerstones (desire, desire denied, wounds, secrets, contradictions) and the [[tyranny-of-motive|Tyranny of Motive]]: the [[ghost|ghost]] anchors an unresolved failure, a [[revenant|revenant]] forces it into the present, and the choice between them is [[growth-vs-transformation|growth or transformation]].

BVX.0061.d: Orson Scott Card's characterization budget: the MICE quotient sets a story's appetite, [[card-hierarchy|the Hierarchy]] allocates it per character, and elaboration of motive spends it. Viewpoint (person, tense, penetration) is declared the telling, not the person.

BVX.0209.d: The wound-to-lie-to-fear-to-shielding chain: an emotional wound seeds [[the-lie|a lie]], the lie manufactures fear, fear builds shielding, and shielding blocks an unmet need until the story forces a choice. Ships as [[wound-card|a fixed eleven-field card]] with a nine-factor [[severity-dial|severity dial]].

BVX.0233.d: Kira-Anne Pelican's six-subfield synthesis: a Big Five profile runs an evolutionary motivation, converted from external to internal by a dated life event. Supplies [[interpersonal-circumplex|the interpersonal circumplex]] and the [[dark-triad|Dark]] and Light Triads.

BVX.0045.d: Victoria Lynn Schmidt's sixteen mythic archetypes, each a [[light-face|light face]] and [[shadow-face|shadow face]] pair, plus two nine-stage growth vectors, [[feminine-journey|the feminine journey]] and [[masculine-journey|the masculine journey]].

BVX.0064.d: Robert McKee's cast-design method: [[true-character|true character]] versus characterization versus subconscious, held together by contradiction, cast across concentric rings by weight on [[cast-map|the Cast Map]].

BVX.0075.d: Rib Davis's nature-plus-nurture build, then the want: a [[super-objective|super-objective]] meets its [[counter-will|counter-will]], and the conflict between the two, forced into choice, reveals rather than develops character.

revenant.d: A present character who forces the reckoning the [[ghost|ghost]] left open. Corbett's pairing is a relational mechanism, a pointer to another character, not an attribute of one ([[BVX.0196]]).

tyranny-of-motive.d: Corbett's warning, built on McKee's line that explaining a character kills her: no single stated cause should ever be presented as *the* reason for an action ([[BVX.0196]]).

card-hierarchy.d: Card's rule that a character's importance is never assigned directly; eight controllable levers (time, choices, focus, frequency, action, sympathy, viewpoint, strangeness) accumulate into walk-on, minor, or major ([[BVX.0061]]).

mice-quotient.d: Card's four story-shape factors, milieu, idea, character, event; whichever dominates sets the story's structural shape and its appetite for characterization ([[BVX.0061]]).

wound-card.d: Puglisi and Ackerman's fixed eleven-field entry: category, examples, needs compromised, [[the-lie|the lie]], fears, behavioral fallout, traits formed, triggers, and opportunities to overcome ([[BVX.0209]]).

the-lie.d: A self-blaming false belief reached through flawed logic while a character is vulnerable. Not the wounding event itself, the lie is what a change arc must actually resolve ([[BVX.0209]]).

severity-dial.d: Nine tunable factors, proximity, responsibility, support, recurrence, compounding events among them, that set how debilitating a given wound is, instead of a flat damage count ([[BVX.0209]]).

interpersonal-circumplex.d: A two-axis grid, agency (status, dominance, control) crossed with communion (warmth, connectedness), giving a character a plottable, context-dependent social position ([[BVX.0233]]).

dark-triad.d: Machiavellianism, narcissism, and subclinical psychopathy, scored against a Light Triad of Kantianism, humanism, and faith in humanity; complex characters carry both, never one pole alone ([[BVX.0233]]).

light-face.d: An archetype's healthy expression, paired with its own [[shadow-face|shadow face]] and asset list; the same archetype, not a different one, under a met versus a denied fear ([[BVX.0045]]).

shadow-face.d: An archetype curdled by a threatened cared-about thing and a denied fear; carries its own named flaw list, the same archetype as its [[light-face|light face]] under pressure ([[BVX.0045]]).

feminine-journey.d: Schmidt's nine-stage growth vector, illusion through betrayal, descent, and rebirth, moving a character toward gaining power ([[BVX.0045]]).

masculine-journey.d: Schmidt's nine-stage growth vector, the call through trials to a death-fork and awaken-or-rebel, moving a character toward surrendering power ([[BVX.0045]]).

growth-vs-transformation.d: Corbett's typed distinction for [[l11-destiny|DESTINY]]: growth digs deeper and wins through will, transformation tears down a wall and wins through insight ([[BVX.0196]]).

counter-will.d: Boal's internal-conflict engine by way of Davis: a want meets its own opposite, and the forced choice between them is what reveals [[l4-will|WILL]] rather than growing it ([[BVX.0075]]).

super-objective.d: Stanislavski's term, by way of Davis: the single, densest want driving a character's active goal-pursuit, [[l6-drive|DRIVE]]'s fuel source ([[BVX.0075]]).

true-character.d: McKee's middle level of self, the choice made under pressure when it costs something, distinct from characterization (the surface) and the subconscious (the buried) ([[BVX.0064]]).

cast-map.d: McKee's concentric-circle allocation: dimensional weight concentrates at the protagonist and thins to nothing at the periphery, a time budget rather than an oversight ([[BVX.0064]]).

stress-threshold.d: Derived statistic, `WILL - WOUND`. How much pressure a character absorbs before the [[l5-wound|wound]]'s lie starts speaking louder than resolve.

collapse-risk.d: Derived statistic, `(WOUND + SHADOW.shadow_density) / 2`. How close a character sits to behavioral collapse under sustained pressure.

truth-exposure-index.d: Derived statistic, `SOCIAL + (10 - EROS.shame_index)`. The primary systemic legibility metric: a score above 15 means the character cannot manage their own signal visibility.

expressive-range.d: Derived statistic, `10 - EROS.armor_index`. What a character can intentionally send, as against Truth Exposure Index, what leaks regardless of intent.

t1-voice.d: Who speaks: person (homodiegetic vs heterodiegetic), level (extra- to metadiegetic), reliability, and time of narration. The TELLING PROFILE's first line; [[BVX.0596]] supplies the CN/EN vocabulary.

t2-focalization.d: Who sees: zero, internal (fixed/variable/multiple), or external focalization, plus the perceptual and informational sub-fields [[BVX.0598]] and [[BVX.0596]] argue T2 should carry. The law: [[who-speaks-vs-who-sees|who speaks is not who sees]].

t3-order.d: Story-time vs discourse-time: analepsis and prolepsis, each with reach and extent. The telling's rearrangement of the ladder's signpost order.

t4-duration.d: The five speeds: scene, summary, stretch, pause, ellipsis. Already wired into the SCENE CARD's `duration` field; [[BVX.0273|Hall]] operationalizes its mimetic end as [[the-distance-dial|the distance dial]].

t5-frequency.d: How often: singulative, repetitive, iterative. Repetitive is trauma's signature, iterative is habit's, mirroring S8 HABIT.

t6-words.d: In what words: diction, syntax, distance policy (cinematic/light/deep), and [[free-indirect-discourse|free indirect discourse]]. Fed hardest by [[BVX.0273]], [[BVX.0084]], and [[BVX.0061]].

t7-feeling.d: With what feeling: tone (the implied author's attitude) and mood (the reader-side atmosphere), recorded as [[the-mood-curve|the mood curve]] per [[BVX.0279]].

t8-thresholds.d: Through what thresholds: paratext, titles, chapter heads, epigraphs, in-world documents. A design surface for movement names and Administration memos.

t9-frames.d: Breaking which frames: metalepsis and the unnatural, narrator-level violations. Normalized as direct address in M9 PORN per the medium grammars.

t10-narratee.d: To whom: the narratee inside the text and the implied reader the text assumes. [[BVX.0279]] supplies the reader-facing half, [[the-three-vs|the three V's]].

t11-medium.d: New T-layer: which channel's grammar re-instruments the telling, M1 to M10 from the medium grammars. Writes `medium`, `grammar_overrides`.

t12-function.d: New T-layer: storyform binding, which throughline the telling serves and its argument role, fed independently from the storyform exactly as L12 and S12 are. Writes `story_point`, `storyform_id`.

BVX.0598.d: The reference-shelf battlefield map of mediation vocabulary: fourteen essays converging on one law, [[who-speaks-vs-who-sees|who speaks is not who sees]]. Source of [[the-mediation-chain|the mediation chain]] (the DNS) and [[the-reflection-axis|the reflection axis]].

BVX.0596.d: Mieke Bal's fabula/story/text cut and her [[the-focalizor|focalizor]] apparatus: [[ef-cf|EF/CF]], perceptible/non-perceptible marking, and [[narrator-focalizer-discrepancy|narrator/focalizer discrepancy]] as a manipulation diagnostic.

BVX.0273.d: Rayne Hall's technique inventory for pushing T2 and T6 to their mimetic ceiling: [[barrier-words|barrier words]] removed, [[the-distance-dial|the distance dial]] named cinematic/light/deep alongside Card ([[BVX.0061]]).

BVX.0084.d: Gloria Kempton's [[the-seven-function-test|seven-function test]] for a line of dialogue, plus [[viewpoint-silence|viewpoint silence]] and strategic tagging as subtext's unnamed mechanism.

BVX.0279.d: Karl Iglesias's seven-emotion taxonomy and [[the-three-vs|the three V's]]: reader emotion, not character emotion, is the target. Supplies [[the-mood-curve|the mood curve]] and [[the-payoff-owed|the payoff owed]].

BVX.0349.d: Alexis Kennedy's counter-voice: distinctiveness over expansiveness, the gutter of implication over inventory. Feeds the setting shelf directly; keyed texture-adjacent here for its microtext and paratext essays.

focalization.d: Who sees, as distinct from who speaks: a fictive entity's subjective view ([[BVX.0596|Bal]]) or, in Genette's second sense, what the reader is denied ([[BVX.0598]]). T2's governing concept.

the-focalizor.d: Bal's term for whoever's vision colors the story: EF (external) or CF (character), marked perceptible or non-perceptible. The narrator never touches the focalized object directly, only through the focalizor.

ef-cf.d: Bal's split of [[the-focalizor|the focalizor]]: EF, an external focalizer outside the story, or CF, a character-focalizer inside it. Proposed as a T2 sub-field alongside the perceptible/non-perceptible marking.

free-indirect-discourse.d: Narrator and character voice fused with no clear marker of the switch; prose's signature instrument (T6), and M1 PROSE's native grammar per the medium grammars.

the-distance-dial.d: T6's diegesis-to-mimesis scale, named cinematic, light, or deep by both [[BVX.0273|Hall]] and [[BVX.0061|Card]]. Show, don't tell is a setting on this dial, not a commandment.

barrier-words.d: Hall's closed verb list, think, wonder, realize, know, that announces a thought is being reported. Removing them is deep PoV's most repeatable technique, and a candidate countable instrument for [[the-distance-dial|the distance dial]].

the-mediation-chain.d: The DNS's three simultaneous dimensions, perception, reflection, and mediation proper, running fabula to focalizor to narrator to words to narratee. Changing one dimension predisposes the other two ([[BVX.0598]]).

the-reflection-axis.d: The DNS's third dimension: a narrator's or character's cognitive, emotive, and normative mark-up of what is perceived, distinct from T1 voice and T2 focalization. No clean home among the Ten Questions; OPEN call 4 asks whether T7 absorbs it.

viewpoint-silence.d: Kempton's tension technique: the viewpoint character visibly not saying what she's thinking. Neither zero, internal, nor external focalization, a focalized character's deliberate non-report, proposed as a T2 sub-value.

the-seven-function-test.d: Kempton's audit: a line of dialogue must characterize, set mood, intensify conflict, move plot, pace the scene, carry setting, or state theme, or it earns no place in the scene.

the-mood-curve.d: Iglesias's per-unit sequence of named reader emotions, interest, curiosity, anticipation, suspense, surprise, thrill, empathy, each with a technique and, if anticipation, [[the-payoff-owed|the payoff owed]]. T7's working content.

the-three-vs.d: Iglesias's taxonomy of why a reader feels anything: Voyeuristic (curiosity about new worlds), Vicarious (identification), Visceral (raw thrill). T10's reader-construction half.

the-payoff-owed.d: Anticipation must resolve into surprise, disappointment, or relief; an unpaid promise reads as broken. Part of [[the-mood-curve|the mood curve]]'s entry format.

narrator-focalizer-discrepancy.d: Bal's diagnostic: a gap between what is narrated (T1) and what is focalized (T2) is where a text manipulates its reader. Proposed as a flag on the TELLING PROFILE.

telling-profile.d: The discourse twin of the storyform: a work's fixed configuration of the Ten Questions' answers, recorded per ladder address, overridable per unit. Instanced by the texture system's twelve-line profile block.

the-telling-line.d: The SCENE CARD's per-scene override of [[telling-profile|the TELLING PROFILE]], T1 plus T2 plus T4 for that scene; the texture system proposes adding a register slot per [[BVX.0084]].

who-speaks-vs-who-sees.t: who speaks is not who sees
who-speaks-vs-who-sees.d: The load-bearing law of the texture layer: a heterodiegetic narrator (T1) can see through one character only (T2 internal fixed). Collapsing the two is the most common craft confusion; [[BVX.0598]] and [[BVX.0596]] both name it the field's central error.

the-translation-grid.d: The texture layer's table of craft vocabulary as compressed T1 x T2 (and T3, T4, T6) configurations: third limited, deep PoV, show don't tell. Not reproduced in the texture system; see the layer doc.

the-ten-questions.d: The texture layer's taxonomy, T1 through T10, every telling as a configuration of ten answers. The texture system restates them as PART B's axes and adds T11 and T12.

g1-label.d: Industry label, marketing label, and critical label, three independent fields, never one slot. Fed by [[BVX.0580]]'s finding that the three routinely diverge.

g2-family.d: Which family a genre belongs to and its polar opposite. Fed by Truby's genre families ([[BVX.0191]]) and Coyne's [[genre-clover|five-leaf clover]] ([[BVX.0236]]).

g3-contract.d: The conventions a genre owes the reader: a component list, criteria steps, [[obligatory-scene|obligatory scenes]]. Fed by [[BVX.0576]], [[BVX.0236]], and [[BVX.0163]].

g4-argument.d: The [[moral-argument|moral argument]] and [[core-binary|core binary]] a genre's whole structure exists to prove, restated as a Thematic Recipe ([[BVX.0191]]).

g5-stance.d: The reader's epistemic position and [[resolution-mode|resolution mode]]: sustained [[the-hesitation|hesitation]], resolves natural, resolves supernatural, or normalized from the start ([[BVX.0614]]).

g6-delivery.d: How the strange enters the text and whether it is explained: [[delivery-mode|delivery mode]], [[portal-quest|portal-quest]], [[immersive-fantasy|immersive]], intrusion, liminal ([[BVX.0599]]).

g7-verisimilitude.d: [[two-verisimilitudes|The two verisimilitudes]] a genre is judged against, the generic regime it licenses internally and the cultural regime everyday belief still holds it to ([[BVX.0580]]).

g8-world.d: The story-world a genre promises to build, [[genre-setting-contract|the genre-setting contract]]: Southern Gothic, western, space opera as setting promises ([[BVX.0191]]).

g9-uptake.d: What this genre calls forth and what answers it next, a [[uptake|genre system]] in Bawarshi and Reiff's sense: pitch calls treatment calls greenlight ([[BVX.0581]]).

g10-audience.d: [[the-icm|The ICM]] a genre builds in an audience before a scene is drafted, plus Dramatica's audience appreciations ([[BVX.0576]], [[BVX.0089]]).

g11-market.d: Cycle, budget tier, and risk position, the industrial planning units Neale finds routinely outrank genre itself ([[BVX.0580]]).

g12-function.d: What this genre does for the Grand Argument, independent of G1 through G11. Fed independently from the storyform, keyed by [[storyform-id|storyform_id]]; mirrors L12, S12, P12, and T12 FUNCTION.

genre-card.d: One per genre in the Command's register: Truby's chapter schema merged with Selbo's field list, name and labels through transcending variants.

genre-contract-instrument.d: One per work: primary genre, overriding and supporting mix, delivery mode, resolution mode, register, and the obligations owed the plot card's P10 line discharges one by one.

moral-argument.d: Truby's claim: each of the fourteen genres is a stated philosophy a story's whole structure exists to prove, never a plot template alone ([[BVX.0191]]).

core-binary.d: A genre's single fundamental-concern sentence (Horror: Religion, Love: the Art of Happiness), doubling as chapter title and rung on Truby's enlightenment ladder ([[BVX.0191]]).

the-hesitation.d: Todorov's fantastic: the reader's sustained, undecided state between a natural and supernatural account of one event. A relation, not a content ([[BVX.0614]]).

resolution-mode.d: How a genre's hesitation settles: sustained, resolves natural (the uncanny), resolves supernatural (the marvelous), or normalized from the start (Kafka's generalized fantastic) ([[BVX.0614]]).

delivery-mode.d: Mendlesohn's variable: how the fantastic enters the narrated world and whether it is explained, distinct from focalization or grammatical person ([[BVX.0599]]).

immersive-fantasy.d: Mendlesohn's second category: the reader is already of the world, no portal, no explanation; a fantasy of thinning rather than discovery ([[BVX.0599]]).

portal-quest.d: Mendlesohn's first category: the reader is led through by a guide-narrator, gradual explanation, reward and restoration at the end ([[BVX.0599]]).

two-verisimilitudes.d: Neale's pair: generic verisimilitude (plausible by the genre's own rules) and cultural verisimilitude (plausible by everyday belief). Every genre balances both ([[BVX.0580]]).

the-inter-textual-relay.d: Posters, trailers, stills, reviews, credit sequences: the industry's own machinery for a film's narrative image, and the primary evidence for what a genre actually was ([[BVX.0580]]).

typified-social-action.d: Miller's founding definition: a genre is a typified rhetorical action that helps constitute the recurrent situation it responds to, not a container for texts ([[BVX.0581]]).

uptake.d: Freadman's mechanism: the conditioned, memoried way one genre's move calls forth a specific genre in response, like a played tennis shot. Selective, not causal ([[BVX.0581]]).

genre-system-term.d: Several genre sets coordinated toward one overarching function (Devitt, Bazerman), one scale in a nested taxonomy running set to system to repertoire to a whole culture's context of genres ([[BVX.0581]]).

meta-genre.d: Giltrow's term: an atmosphere-level text or talk, a style bible, a showrunner's tone memo, that teaches and stabilizes how a genre gets used, sitting above genre and register both ([[BVX.0581]]).

the-icm.d: Selbo's idealized cognitive model: an audience's mental space for a genre, built from schematic, specific, and relevant knowledge, before a scene is drafted ([[BVX.0576]]).

overriding-genre.d: The genre that dominates a story's frame and must fully satisfy its own criteria; other genres support it (Neale's genre hybrid) ([[BVX.0576]]).

supporting-genre.d: A genre stacked beneath the overriding genre; counts toward a hybrid only if its own criteria are substantially met, not merely gestured at ([[BVX.0576]]).

the-fourteen-genres.d: Truby's set: Horror, Action, Myth, Memoir/Coming-of-Age, Fantasy, Detective/Thriller, Love, Science Fiction, Crime, Comedy, Western, Gangster, each a moral argument proved through a fixed schema ([[BVX.0191]]).

mode-vs-genre.d: Bordwell's distinction, via Selbo: mode is the delivery vehicle (animation, documentary, mini-series); it says nothing about content. Mode is never genre ([[BVX.0576]]).

genre-setting-contract.d: The spine's L7-to-setting touchpoint: Southern Gothic, western, space opera are genres that ARE setting promises, not decoration on top of one ([[BVX.0191]]).

the-four-vocabularies.d: Snyder's ten, Coyne's clover, Selbo's sixteen, and Truby's fourteen genres: four independently arrived-at genre lists for one reader-contract territory, none substituting for another.

BVX.1123.d: Lajos Egri's 1946 craft book: a character is [[the-bone-structure|the bone structure]], physiology, sociology, psychology; [[the-premise|the premise]] is the one sentence the whole play must prove; [[strength-of-will|strength of will]] defines [[the-pivotal-character|the pivotal character]].

BVX.1124.d: Campbell's monomyth compressed into [[the-twelve-stages|twelve stages]] and eight archetypes as [[archetypes-as-masks|masks]], including [[the-ordeal|the Ordeal]]'s death-and-rebirth and [[the-repeat-turn|a second, harder Resurrection]].

BVX.1125.t: Brody (Save the Cat! Writes a Novel)
BVX.1125.d: Snyder's fifteen beats re-keyed to percentages of manuscript length, wrapped in an A Story/B Story want-need split and [[the-ingredient-triad|the ingredient triad]], exactly three required elements per genre.

BVX.1126.d: The rival map's root ancestor, read from the primary text (trans. Sachs): [[hamartia|hamartia]], [[peripeteia|peripeteia]], and [[anagnorisis|anagnorisis]] drive the tragic plot, and [[catharsis|catharsis]] is completed eighteen chapters later in [[wonder-telos|wonder]].

BVX.1127.d: Adult attachment theory as three styles, secure, anxious, avoidant, run by one evolved system; [[protest-behaviors|protest behaviors]], [[deactivating-strategies|deactivating strategies]], and [[the-secure-base|the secure base]]'s buffering effect.

the-bone-structure.d: Egri's tridimensional outline, physiology, sociology, psychology, 27 named fields under three headings; the character shelf's earliest complete checklist ([[BVX.1123]]).

strength-of-will.d: Not toughness, the capacity to decide and act; a weak character is one who cannot make a decision, Egri's clearest ancestor of [[l4-will|L4 WILL]] ([[BVX.1123]]).

the-pivotal-character.d: The protagonist, forced into the role by necessity, not choice; grows less than other characters because the decision predates the curtain ([[BVX.1123]]).

the-premise.d: One sentence, character, conflict, conclusion, that the whole play must prove; one generation before Davis's [[super-objective|super-objective]] ([[BVX.1123]]).

hamartia.d: Missing the mark, archery imagery, never badness of character; corrects the tragic-flaw tradition traced to Butcher's 1895 mistranslation ([[BVX.1126]]).

peripeteia.d: The change to the opposite of the things being done, the oldest named reversal mechanism the house holds, mapping onto [[p4-turn|P4 TURN]] ([[BVX.1126]]).

anagnorisis.d: A change from ignorance to recognition, best when simultaneous with a reversal; Ch.16 ranks discovery forms least to most artful, mapping onto [[p7-reveal|P7 REVEAL]] ([[BVX.1126]]).

catharsis.d: The washing-away of pity and fear, named once and never explained until [[wonder-telos|wonder]] completes it eighteen chapters later; a live scholarly problem, not a settled house term ([[BVX.1126]]).

wonder-telos.d: Ekplexis, the knocking-away of habitual judgment; Sachs's central claim that tragedy's actual telos is wonder, not a guaranteed lesson ([[BVX.1126]]).

protest-behaviors.d: The anxious response to perceived threat, silent treatment, monitoring, manufactured jealousy, aimed at restoring attention ([[BVX.1127]]).

deactivating-strategies.d: The avoidant response: focusing on a partner's flaws, idealizing an ex, comparing to alternatives, creating distance; regulation, not disinterest ([[BVX.1127]]).

the-secure-base.d: A consistently available partner as a base to return to and a shield against outside stress; Coan's fMRI hand-holding study anchors the buffering effect experimentally ([[BVX.1127]]).

archetypes-as-masks.d: Vogler's own phrase, from Propp: the eight archetypes worn temporarily as needed, not fixed roles; any character, including the Hero, can trade masks mid-scene ([[BVX.1124]]).

the-twelve-stages.d: Vogler's compression of Campbell's monomyth into a practical map any story can shuffle, skip, or merge, from Ordinary World to Return with the Elixir ([[BVX.1124]]).

the-ordeal.d: A literal or symbolic death confronting the hero's greatest fear, staged so the hero 'must die or appear to die'; Resurrection stages a second, harder pass before Return ([[BVX.1124]]).

the-ingredient-triad.d: Every one of Brody's ten genres reduces to exactly three required ingredients; a fast completeness check against a genre draft ([[BVX.1125]]).

the-repeat-turn.d: Vogler's Resurrection forcing a second full value-in/turn/value-out pass before Return, a need [[p9-stakes|P9 STAKES/ESCALATION]]'s single 'trend up' rule doesn't yet name ([[BVX.1124]]).

multi-pov.d: Brody's allowance for one full fifteen-beat instance per POV hero, layered on a shared timeline, proven on the Institutionalized/Help worked example ([[BVX.1125]]).
